title: Metallic Materials — Bend Test
technical_committee: MED 04 (Mechanical Testing of Metals Sectional Committee)
scope: This standard specifies the method for determining the ability of metallic materials to undergo plastic deformation in bending. It applies to test pieces taken from metallic products (sheets, strips, plates, bars, sections, wire) as specified in the relevant product standard.
description: IS 1599:2019 (Fourth Revision) establishes the technical principles, testing equipment, test piece geometry, and defect evaluation for bend tests on metallic materials. It is identical to ISO 7438:2016. The bend test consists of subjecting a test piece of round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section to plastic deformation by bending around a former/mandrel without reversing the direction of flexure, followed by optical examination for surface fissures or cracks.

key_requirements.requirement: The test shall be carried out at ambient temperature between 10°C and 35°C unless otherwise specified.

key_requirements.parameter: Edge Rounding of Rectangular Test Pieces
key_requirements.requirement: The edges of rectangular test pieces shall be rounded with a radius (r) not exceeding 0.1 times the thickness (0.1a) to prevent premature corner notch failure.
The diameter of the bending mandrel or former shall conform strictly to the product specification ratio (d = k * a).
key_requirements.acceptable_limit: As specified in product standard (e.g. 1a to 5a)

key_requirements.requirement: The test piece shall be bent to the angle specified in the relevant product standard (typically 90°, 120°, or 180°).

After bending to the prescribed angle, the outer convex surface and sides of the test piece shall be visually inspected; no cracks, fissures, or tears visible without magnifying aids shall be permitted.
key_requirements.acceptable_limit: Zero visible cracks on convex surface
key_requirements.permissible_limit: Cracks at corners < 0.1a ignored unless origin is material flaw

key_requirements.requirement: The bending load shall be applied smoothly and continuously at a rate not exceeding 30 mm/min to avoid dynamic shock loading.

sections.title: Scope
sections.content: This standard specifies the method for determining the ability of metallic materials to undergo plastic deformation in bending. This standard applies to test pieces taken from metallic products, as specified in the relevant product standard. It is not applicable to full cross-section tests on tubes and welded joints, which are covered by other dedicated standards.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.content: The following referenced documents are indispensable for the application of this document: ISO 7438:2016 Metallic materials — Bend test, IS 1608 (Part 1) Metallic materials — Tensile testing, IS 1786 High strength deformed steel bars and wires for concrete reinforcement.

sections.title: Symbols and Designations
sections.content: Key symbols used in the bend test: a = thickness or diameter of test piece (or diameter of inscribed circle for polygonal section); b = width of test piece; L = total length of test piece; l = distance between supports (l = d + 3a ± 0.5a); d = diameter of the mandrel or former; r = radius of edges of test piece; alpha = angle of bend.

sections.title: Principle of Test
sections.content: The bend test consists of subjecting a test piece of round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section to plastic deformation by bending around a former of known radius without reversing the direction of flexure. The operation is continued until one of the specified conditions (bend angle, parallel legs, or contact of legs) is reached.

sections.title: Testing Equipment
sections.content: The test shall be carried out in testing machines or presses equipped with the following devices: a) Bending device with two supports and a former/mandrel; b) Bending device with a V-block and a former; c) Bending device with a clamp (flanging/wrapping device). The supports shall have a radius of curvature between 1 mm and 10 times the test piece thickness and must be hardened to prevent indentations.

subsections.title: Bending Device with Supports and Mandrel
subsections.content: The distance between the supports (l) shall be l = d + 3a unless otherwise stated in the product standard. The former shall move perpendicularly to the span, pressing at mid-length between supports.

sections.title: Test Piece Preparation
sections.content: Round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section test pieces shall be used. For products with thickness <= 25 mm, the test piece thickness shall be the full product thickness. Edges of rectangular pieces shall be rounded with a radius not exceeding 0.1a to eliminate machining burrs and stress concentrations.

subsections.title: Sampling and Orientation
subsections.content: The test piece shall be prepared in accordance with the specifications of the relevant product standard, taking transverse or longitudinal samples as prescribed.

sections.title: Procedure
sections.content: The test is conducted at ambient temperature between 10°C and 35°C. The test piece is placed symmetrically on supports and bent by smoothly applying force through the mandrel. The bend angle (alpha) is measured either directly from the angle of the bent legs or by closing until legs are parallel (alpha = 180°).

subsections.title: Bending Rate and Method
subsections.content: The speed of the mandrel during bending shall not exceed 30 mm/min. For bending to 180° parallel legs, intermediate bending on supports is followed by direct pressing between parallel platens.

sections.title: Interpretation of Results
sections.content: The evaluation of the bend test shall be carried out in accordance with the requirements of the product standard. When these requirements are not specified, absence of surface cracks visible without magnifying aids on the tension side (convex surface) after bending is considered as evidence that the test piece passed the test.
